title.narrative: Providing WASH and Child Protection Services for Communities Affected by the 7.3 Earthquake in Vanuatu

description.narrative: The project aims to provide urgent life-saving integrated WASH and Child Protection services to communities affected by the 7.3 earthquake while strengthening resilience within the community. The project aims to reach approximately 7,000 individuals, including 5,000 children, with targeted interventions in water, sanitation, hygiene (WASH), and child protection.Impact:Deliver life-saving WASH services and ensure the safety and well-being of children, providing psychosocial support and protection from abuse in the aftermath of the earthquake. AssessmentsRapid field visits were conducted post-earthquake to identify urgent WASH and protection gaps. There are significant damage to water systems, including reservoirs, pipes, and water tanks in Port Vila and surrounding areas. There is also water disruption at the health facility.Interviews with families highlighted increased risks of abuse and mental distress among children. WASH: The project will support the overall WASH cluster response target of over 5,000 people. UNICEF will support the cluster on life saving response, coordination, assessments, information management and reporting of the response.Key Activities:Emergency water trucking to affected areas for over 5,000 peopleDistribution of 750 hygiene kits, household filters, and water storage containers for 3,750Dissemination of safe water treatment information to prevent waterborne diseases.Provision of 10 water pumps and installation of bladder systems in evacuation centers.Repairs to damaged reservoirs, pipes, and water distribution points to restore water supplyInstallation of emergency latrines with handwashing facilities in 10 schools, health centers, and evacuation centers.Dissemination of critical hygiene messages through SMS, radio, and community platforms, reaching 20,000 individuals. Child Protection: The project will support the overall Child Protection in Emergencies sub-cluster response with a target of 40,000 people of which UNICEF direct beneficiaries are 5,000 children and their care givers. UNICEF will support the cluster on coordination, assessments, information management, service delivery and reporting of the response. Key Activities:Messaging to parents on managing child distress and accessing support services.5,000 People accessing protection activities and/or services through child-friendly spacesProvision of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS)Support for community-based psychosocial activities and establishment of child-friendly spaces (10 spaces).Strengthening referral mechanisms for vulnerable children requiring advanced care.Awareness campaigns on risk mitigation and protection for women and children
